recommendation.text: Resting bids and alerts can't be told apart (an edge under about 3.2% wouldn't show). Prefer alerts: your cash stays free and earning.

Selling stink-bid fills into the rebound by hand beat random buys of the same coin by 6.3% per fill (95% CI +2.8% to +9.9%). After Robinhood costs, a flip made +4.8% on average (+4.8% on the Robinhood-route proxy, F3). It held in both halves, without the biggest month and crash, and on Robinhood-like prices. The sheet shows the flip target. [1541 fills, month-block clusters G = 58, G* = 14.5]
Can't tell; the sheet uses plain volatility-scaled levels.

fixed_sentences.text: A bid's discount is not a gain by itself. If prices are unpredictable, a bid 30% below the price buys the same expected value as buying now, minus what the coin earns while you wait; in a crash that gaps through your price, it buys less. Only a quick rebound after the wick can pay for the wait.

Bids fill together. On the worst day, 95% of the live bids in the study's main universe filled the same day. Size the whole ladder as one position you are willing to hold through a further 50-80% fall. [day 2025-10-10: 94 of 99 live P1 bids on U-Q1; on the Robinhood-route proxy (F3): 95% on 2025-10-10 (94 of 99)]

A fill is not a bottom: 27.3% of past fills were 50% or more below the fill price a year later, against 28.4% for random buys of the same coins. [1329 P1 fills with a year observed; Binance spot fills, F3 not computed]

Coin-specific collapses (LUNA, FTT, OM) look like ordinary wicks on the first day; a resting order cannot read the news. Cancel a coin's bids on news about the coin itself (a hack, exploit, depeg, delisting or regulatory action).

Most past fills came when the coin's MoneyLine was already red; a fill buys against your own trend signal. Decide before the fill which rule governs the position. The sheet uses the replicated pre-October-2026 MoneyLine. [computed: 62.8% of P1 fills with a defined state were red at placement (970 red, 574 green, 0 undefined); F3 fills: 63.8% red (870 red, 494 green)]

Capacity: assume every rung fills on the same day, and keep each order within the size cap (a quarter of the 10th percentile of past seller-initiated dollars printed below the level on Binance spot during the wick, from the first trade below it until it trades back above or 60 minutes pass): rung k = 6: 10th percentile $18,823, cap about $4,706 per order; rung k = 8: 10th percentile $20,872, cap about $5,218 per order; rung k = 10: 10th percentile $24,282, cap about $6,071 per order.

descriptive_sentences: Descriptive only. Over 90 days, coins bought through stink bids did 3.5% (95% CI -19.9% to +13.0% for the difference) worse than the same coins bought at random times outside the six months around each fill. An edge under about 20-40% could not be detected, and the comparison also reflects whether the crashes fell in bear or bull stretches. [1513 fills, quarter-block clusters G = 27, G* = 12.9; MDE computed here 24.7%; on the Robinhood-route proxy (F3): -5.2% (95% CI -20.9% to +10.5%; 1339 fills, quarter-block clusters G = 26, G* = 12.4)]
Random buys here exclude the six months around each fill, so the comparison also reflects whether crashes fell in bear or bull stretches. (K1c, regime timing alone: -6.1% per 90 days)

Descriptive only. Fast wicks were 4.3% per fill (95% CI -1.8% to +10.2% for the difference) better than slow slides to the same depth. A difference under about 6-10% per fill could not be detected. [1054 fills, month-block clusters G = 45, G* = 11.1; episode fixed effects; MDE computed here 8.2%; on the Robinhood-route proxy (F3): +2.9% (95% CI -3.9% to +9.6%; 946 fills, month-block clusters G = 44, G* = 10.7)]

Descriptive only. A year after a fill, 27.3% of fills on large, long-listed coins and 46.5% on other top-100 coins were 50% or more below the fill price; at the same volatility the gap was +12.9 points (95% CI +4.6 to +21.2). Neither LUNA (kept out by listing age) nor FTT (kept out by Binance volume rank) was in the large, long-listed group, so this says nothing about fraud collapses of large coins. In the 12-month row, where LUNA is included, the gap was +8.4 points. The study did not test a real-revenue filter. [4230 fills; two-way coin x quarter clusters, G_coin = 355, G_quarter = 26, t at 25 df; Binance spot fills only, F3 not computed on U-B (prereg Addendum 1, A1.7)]

Flip or own is a choice about whether you want to hold the coin, not about stink-bid skill. The study's evidence on the bid is the same for both. [shared premium (the alert buyer's price 72 h later): +5.5% (95% CI +2.6% to +8.4%; 1541 fills, month-block clusters G = 58, G* = 14.5); on the Robinhood-route proxy (F3): +5.7% (95% CI +2.4% to +9.1%; 1361 fills, month-block clusters G = 54, G* = 13.8); return from 72 h to 90 days against T-bills: +10.6% (95% CI -7.0% to +28.2%; 1513 fills, quarter-block clusters G = 27, G* = 12.9); on the Robinhood-route proxy (F3): +8.7% (95% CI -6.1% to +23.5%; 1339 fills, quarter-block clusters G = 26, G* = 12.4)]

Found after the controls stage, before any outcome (prereg Addendum 2, A2.5): the runner took the condensed K3 block of controls/summary.json for the K3 calibration, so H2R's simulation-calibrated rule would have been dropped. Fixed in stinkbid_run._find_calibration (only a full calibration, k3_calibration.json; a summary rule that disagrees closes the gate). The controls marker's calibrated_tests reads [] for the same reason; the gate recomputes it from the files at every later stage (H2R). No control result or file changed; nothing reran.

post-results corrections found by the outcome audit and verified independently (reporting only; no verdict, test statistic or gate changes): (1) the size cap Q_max used seller dollars summed over the order's whole life instead of the fill's own capacity window (draft 7.3, 8.3), overstating it 17-22 times; (2) H4's printed MDE used a single test's critical value instead of its four-method Bonferroni (1.17%, not 0.94%); (3) H4's 'without the top month-block' row used M7's own month-blocks instead of the shared partition (A1.8); (4) prereg 12 and A1.7: F3 numbers beside the answer's Binance numbers, 'F3 not computed' notes, G and G* with recommendation intervals, U-C rows labelled hindsight, H4's missing U-C row stated.
